passage:
The following text is from Mark Twain's 1883 memoir *Life on the Mississippi*. Twain grew up in a small town on the Mississippi River.

When I was a boy, there was but one permanent ambition among my comrades in our village … on the west bank of the Mississippi River. That was, to be a steamboatman. We had transient ambitions of other sorts, but they were only transient. When a circus came and went, it left us all burning to become clowns; … now and then we had a hope that if we lived and were good, God would permit us to be pirates. These ambitions faded out, each in its turn; but the ambition to be a steamboatman always remained.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe a childhood goal that, unlike the boys' other ambitions, never lost its appeal
option_b: To explain how the narrator eventually became a steamboatman
option_c: To compare the dangers of working on a steamboat with those of performing in a circus
option_d: To criticize the adults of the village for discouraging the boys' dreams
explanation_en:
The text names one “permanent ambition,” to be a steamboatman, and contrasts it with “transient” ambitions such as becoming clowns or pirates, which “faded out, each in its turn.” Its purpose is to show that this one goal lasted while the others did not, as choice A says.

Choice B is wrong because the text never says whether or how the narrator achieved his ambition. Choice C is wrong because the text mentions the circus only as a passing ambition and discusses no dangers. Choice D is wrong because adults and their opinions are not mentioned at all.

passage:
The following text is from Willa Cather's 1913 novel *O Pioneers!* A little boy is crying on a town sidewalk because his kitten is stuck at the top of a pole. He sees his older sister coming toward him.

His sister was a tall, strong girl, and she walked rapidly and resolutely, as if she knew exactly where she was going and what she was going to do next. She wore a man’s long ulster (not as if it were an affliction, but as if it were very comfortable and belonged to her; carried it like a young soldier), and a round plush cap, tied down with a thick veil. She had a serious, thoughtful face, and her clear, deep blue eyes were fixed intently on the distance, without seeming to see anything, as if she were in trouble.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To explain why the boy's kitten climbed to the top of the pole
option_b: To describe the harsh winter weather in the town
option_c: To introduce a character by emphasizing her strength, confidence, and seriousness
option_d: To show that the sister is embarrassed by the coat she is wearing
explanation_en:
The whole text describes the sister: she is “tall, strong,” walks “resolutely,” wears her coat “like a young soldier,” and has a “serious, thoughtful face.” Its purpose is to introduce her and stress these qualities, as choice C says.

Choice A is wrong because the text says nothing about how the kitten got onto the pole. Choice B is wrong because the weather is not described in this text. Choice D is wrong because the narrator says the opposite: she wears the man's coat “not as if it were an affliction, but as if it were very comfortable and belonged to her.”

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda mushukcha ustunga qanday chiqib qolgani aytilmaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: bu matnda ob-havo tasvirlanmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: hikoyachi buning aksini aytadi — u erkaklar paltosini “azob-uqubatdek emas, balki juda qulay va o‘ziniki bo‘lgandek” kiyib yuradi.

passage: Nearly every musical instrument needs a person to play it. __The aeolian harp, however, is played by the wind.__ Its strings are stretched across a long wooden box that is placed in an open window or on a hilltop. As air moves across the strings, they vibrate and produce soft, shifting chords that no human hand controls.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It describes how the aeolian harp is built.
option_b: It argues that instruments played by the wind sound better than those played by people.
option_c: It gives an example that supports the claim made in the first sentence.
option_d: It introduces an exception to the general statement in the first sentence, which the rest of the text explains.
explanation_en:
The first sentence says nearly every instrument needs a person to play it. The underlined sentence, beginning with “however,” introduces an instrument that does not: the aeolian harp is played by the wind. The rest of the text explains how this works. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the harp's construction is described in the next sentence, not the underlined one. Choice B is wrong because the text never compares the sound of wind-played and human-played instruments. Choice C is wrong because the harp does not support the first sentence's claim; it is an exception to it.

Matnning qolgan qismi bu qanday ishlashini tushuntiradi. D javob aynan shu vazifani ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: arfaning tuzilishi tagiga chizilgan jumlada emas, keyingi jumlada tasvirlanadi. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda shamol va odam chaladigan cholg‘ularning ovozi solishtirilmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: arfa birinchi jumladagi fikrni tasdiqlamaydi, aksincha, undan istisno hisoblanadi.

passage:
The following text is from Frederick Douglass's 1845 autobiography *Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave*. As a boy, Douglass has overheard his enslaver, Mr. Auld, order his wife to stop teaching Douglass to read, because learning would make Douglass unfit to be a slave.

These words sank deep into my heart, stirred up sentiments within that lay slumbering, and called into existence an entirely new train of thought. It was a new and special revelation, explaining dark and mysterious things, with which my youthful understanding had struggled, but struggled in vain. I now understood what had been to me a most perplexing difficulty—to wit, the white man’s power to enslave the black man. It was a grand achievement, and I prized it highly. From that moment, I understood the pathway from slavery to freedom.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a painful memory and then explains why the narrator tried to forget it.
option_b: It presents the narrator's emotional reaction to words he overheard and then identifies the insight those words gave him.
option_c: It summarizes Mr. Auld's argument and then offers evidence that the argument was false.
option_d: It contrasts the narrator's early hopes for freedom with the disappointment he felt later.
explanation_en:
The text first describes how Mr. Auld's words affected Douglass (they “sank deep into my heart” and started “an entirely new train of thought”). It then states what he learned from them: he now understood “the white man’s power to enslave the black man” and “the pathway from slavery to freedom.” Choice B describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because Douglass treasures the insight (“I prized it highly”) rather than trying to forget the moment. Choice C is wrong because Douglass does not argue that Mr. Auld was wrong; he says the words revealed a truth to him. Choice D is wrong because the text moves from confusion to understanding, not from hope to disappointment.
explanation_uz:
Matn avval janob Old so‘zlari Duglasga qanday ta’sir qilganini tasvirlaydi (ular “yuragimga chuqur botdi” va “butunlay yangi fikrlar oqimini” uyg‘otdi). So‘ng u bu so‘zlardan nimani anglaganini aytadi: endi u “oq tanlining qora tanlini qul qilish qudrati”ni va “qullikdan ozodlikka olib boruvchi yo‘l”ni tushundi. B javob shu tuzilishni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: Duglas bu lahzani unutishga urinmaydi, aksincha, anglaganini “juda qadrlagan.” C noto‘g‘ri: Duglas janob Oldni nohaq deb isbotlashga urinmaydi; u bu so‘zlar unga haqiqatni ochib berganini aytadi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn umiddan hafsalasi pir bo‘lishga emas, chalkashlikdan tushunishga qarab boradi.

passage:
The following text is from W. E. B. Du Bois's 1903 book *The Souls of Black Folk*.

Between me and the other world there is ever an unasked question: unasked by some through feelings of delicacy; by others through the difficulty of rightly framing it. All, nevertheless, flutter round it. __They approach me in a half-hesitant sort of way, eye me curiously or compassionately, and then, instead of saying directly, How does it feel to be a problem? they say, I know an excellent colored man in my town; or, I fought at Mechanicsville; or, Do not these Southern outrages make your blood boil?__ At these I smile, or am interested, or reduce the boiling to a simmer, as the occasion may require. To the real question, How does it feel to be a problem? I answer seldom a word.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It shows that most people eventually ask the author their real question directly.
option_b: It illustrates, with specific examples, the indirect ways people approach the question mentioned in the first sentence.
option_c: It explains why the author refuses to answer any questions from strangers.
option_d: It introduces a new topic that is unrelated to the unasked question.
explanation_en:
The first sentence describes an “unasked question,” and the second says people “flutter round it.” The underlined sentence shows what this looks like: “instead of saying directly” what they mean, people offer remarks such as “I know an excellent colored man in my town.” It gives concrete examples of the indirect approach, as choice B says.

Choice A is wrong because the underlined sentence stresses that people do not ask the question directly. Choice C is wrong because the author does respond to these remarks (“I smile, or am interested”); what he seldom answers is the unspoken question, and the underlined sentence does not explain his reasons. Choice D is wrong because the examples are directly connected to the unasked question.
explanation_uz:

U bilvosita yondashuvning aniq misollarini keltiradi — to‘g‘ri javob B.

C noto‘g‘ri: muallif bu gaplarga javob beradi (“jilmayaman yoki qiziqib qolaman”); u kamdan-kam javob beradigan narsa — aytilmagan savol, va tagiga chizilgan jumla buning sababini tushuntirmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: misollar so‘ralmagan savol bilan bevosita bog‘liq.

passage: In the 1950s, some scholars argued that the remote islands of the Pacific had been settled mostly by accident, by canoes blown off course in storms. In 1976, however, a crew sailed a traditionally designed double-hulled canoe from Hawaii to Tahiti, a distance of more than 4,000 kilometers, without compasses or charts, finding their way by the stars, the ocean swells, and the flight of birds. The voyage showed that deliberate long-distance navigation without instruments was possible, and many scholars now view the settlement of the Pacific as the result of planned voyages.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a voyage and then explains why the voyage failed to reach its destination.
option_b: It compares two methods of navigation and argues that one is more accurate than the other.
option_c: It presents a debate among scholars and concludes that the debate cannot be settled.
option_d: It presents an earlier explanation, describes a voyage that challenged it, and notes how scholars' views changed as a result.
explanation_en:
The text opens with an earlier conclusion (the islands were settled by accident), then describes the 1976 voyage that showed instrument-free navigation was possible, and ends by noting that many scholars now see settlement as planned. Choice D describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because the voyage succeeded; it is offered as evidence of what was possible. Choice B is wrong because the text does not compare the accuracy of two navigation methods. Choice C is wrong because the text reports that many scholars have changed their view, rather than concluding that the question cannot be settled.
explanation_uz:
Matn avvalgi xulosa bilan boshlanadi (orollarga tasodifan odamlar joylashgan), so‘ng asboblarsiz suzish mumkinligini ko‘rsatgan 1976-yilgi sayohatni tasvirlaydi va ko‘plab olimlar endi orollarga joylashishni rejali sayohatlar natijasi deb bilishini aytib tugaydi. D javob shu tuzilishni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: sayohat muvaffaqiyatli bo‘lgan va nima mumkinligining dalili sifatida keltirilgan. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda ikki xil yo‘l topish usulining aniqligi solishtirilmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda masalani hal qilib bo‘lmaydi degan xulosa yo‘q, aksincha, ko‘plab olimlar fikrini o‘zgartirgani aytiladi.

passage:
The following text is from the 1872 edition of Charles Darwin's *On the Origin of Species*, a book first published in 1859.

When on board H.M.S. Beagle, as naturalist, I was much struck with certain facts in the distribution of the organic beings inhabiting South America, and in the geological relations of the present to the past inhabitants of that continent. … On my return home, it occurred to me, in 1837, that something might perhaps be made out on this question by patiently accumulating and reflecting on all sorts of facts which could possibly have any bearing on it. After five years' work I allowed myself to speculate on the subject, and drew up some short notes; these I enlarged in 1844 into a sketch of the conclusions, which then seemed to me probable: from that period to the present day I have steadily pursued the same object. __I hope that I may be excused for entering on these personal details, as I give them to show that I have not been hasty in coming to a decision.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It acknowledges that the preceding account is personal and explains that it is meant to show how carefully the author reached his conclusions.
option_b: It apologizes for conclusions that the author now believes he reached too quickly.
option_c: It introduces the facts about South America that the author will discuss in later chapters.
option_d: It suggests that the author's personal experiences are more important than the facts he collected.
explanation_en:
Before the underlined sentence, Darwin recounts his own history: years of “patiently accumulating” facts, waiting five years before speculating, and pursuing the subject “steadily” ever since. The underlined sentence admits that these are “personal details” and explains why he included them: “to show that I have not been hasty in coming to a decision.” Choice A captures this function.

Choice B is wrong because Darwin says the opposite: he was not hasty, and he asks to be excused only for including personal details. Choice C is wrong because the facts about South America are mentioned in the first sentence, not introduced by the underlined one. Choice D is wrong because Darwin presents his personal history as evidence of the care he took in studying facts, not as more important than those facts.

Tagiga chizilgan jumlada u bular “shaxsiy tafsilotlar” ekanini tan oladi va ularni nima uchun keltirganini tushuntiradi: “qaror qabul qilishda shoshilmaganimni ko‘rsatish uchun.” A javob shu vazifani ifodalaydi.

passage: Restorers of old paintings once routinely removed yellowed varnish from canvases, confident that they were revealing the colors the artist had intended. Some art historians now question that confidence. __Pigments themselves change over the centuries—some blues fade, some reds darken—so a freshly cleaned painting may display colors that no one, not even the artist, ever saw.__ These historians do not argue that cleaning should stop, but they urge restorers to describe their work as an interpretation rather than a return to an original state.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It describes the method restorers use to remove varnish from paintings.
option_b: It presents evidence that cleaning damages paintings and should therefore be stopped.
option_c: It gives a reason for the doubt that the historians express in the previous sentence.
option_d: It explains why restorers originally became confident that cleaning reveals an artist's colors.
explanation_en:
The previous sentence says some historians “question that confidence”—the belief that cleaning reveals the artist's intended colors. The underlined sentence explains why: the pigments themselves have changed, so the cleaned colors may not be the original ones. Choice C describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the sentence is about how pigments change, not about how varnish is removed. Choice B is wrong because the final sentence states that the historians “do not argue that cleaning should stop,” and the underlined sentence says nothing about damage caused by cleaning. Choice D is wrong because the sentence undermines the restorers' confidence rather than explaining where it came from.

Tagiga chizilgan jumla buning sababini tushuntiradi: bo‘yoqlarning o‘zi vaqt o‘tib o‘zgargan, shuning uchun tozalangan ranglar asl ranglar bo‘lmasligi mumkin. C javob shu vazifani ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: jumla lakni qanday olib tashlash haqida emas, bo‘yoqlar qanday o‘zgarishi haqida. B noto‘g‘ri: oxirgi jumlada tarixchilar “tozalashni to‘xtatish kerak deb aytmaydi” deyilgan, tagiga chizilgan jumlada esa tozalash zarari haqida gap yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: jumla restavratorlarning ishonchi qayerdan kelganini tushuntirmaydi, aksincha, uni zaiflashtiradi.
